title: Retry storm: it never comes back
brief: Yesterday a 5-second traffic spike took this API down, and it stayed down long after traffic went back to normal. Run it: it's fine at 4.3k rps. Then replay the spike with spike(multiplier=2, seconds=5) and watch it fail to recover. Make it recover on its own.

requirements: You can ship a new client: change its retry policy (retries, retry budget, backoff), but keep retrying: phones have flaky networks
After a 2x spike for 5 s, every check is green again within 15 s
variants.twist: Replay it: spike(multiplier=2, seconds=5), then wait 15 s. All checks must be green again without touching anything.

requirements: Millions of old phones retry 3 times, no budget, no backoff, and won't update
After a 2x spike for 5 s, every check is green again within 15 s
variants.twist: Replay it: spike(multiplier=2, seconds=5), then wait 15 s. All checks must be green again without touching anything.

hints: During the spike some requests fail. What does each client do when a request fails, and what does that do to the load?

With 3 retries, a server that fails everything gets up to 4x the traffic, so it can't drain even after users go back to normal. Try backoff alone first: does it help? Then cap how many retries clients may send, or turn the excess away early and cheaply.

New app: set the client's retry_budget to 10% (20% isn't enough here; backoff on top is fine, backoff alone doesn't recover). Old clients: put an API gateway in front of the load balancer with rate_limit_rps about 4500, so the services never queue past their timeout.
_notes: Starter: client (retries 3) -> LB -> 5 services (5k/s) -> KV: $1.43. Steady 4.3k: p99 ~30 ms. Spike 2x for 5 s, then 30 s at normal: stuck at p99 ~4.4 s and ~0.8% errors (metastable). The client sees ~30% failures (API drops + its own 2 s timeout), so retries add ~1.8k rps: 6.1k on a 5k service, and the queue never drains. Exponential backoff alone: still stuck (it spreads retries out, it doesn't remove them). Retry budget 20%: still stuck; 10%: back to green. Gateway 4500 with the old clients: recovers, $1.48. Brute force: 6 services recover but cost $1.53. Real fixes, all worth naming: retry budgets, exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breakers, load shedding at the edge, and making retries idempotent. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
